cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Admit You’re Hurt
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit hurt, fear, or disappointment before you reveal that you feel it too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When Mum cancelled our birthday dinner, were you disappointed? Please answer about yourself first; I don't want us guessing at each other.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's another question, not an answer. Take your time. What did you do after she called?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the supermarket while I was putting the candles back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So did I. I told the cashier it was hay fever. Don't write that off as silly, please; I still haven't managed to return the cake.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1/A3 control disclosure order as a careful interviewer; A5 reveals matching tears only after B4 and preempts dismissal.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 reverses the question; A3 demands a concrete account; B4's supermarket tears trigger A5's own admission.

relationship.evidence: B2 initially protects vulnerability with reciprocity, then admits a specific hurt.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from interviewing to sharing an unfinished return task caused by the same disappointment.

specificity.evidence: A1 names Mum's cancelled birthday dinner; B4 candles and A5 cake fit that event.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 now attributes tears to hay fever coherently rather than equating candles with allergies.
